The problem is a design-by-angle-of-twist for a solid circular shaft under pure torsion.
Assumptions: small-deformation, linear-elastic, homogeneous isotropic solid circular shaft, no stress concentrations, uniform cross-section over the full length, pure torsion with no axial or transverse loads, steady-state loading.
The shaft is made of 6061-T6 aluminum with shear modulus G = 25,939.8 MPa.
The applied torque is T = 1,000,000 N·mm, constant along the length.
The shaft length is L = 1500 mm.
The maximum allowable angle of twist at the free end relative to the fixed end is φ_allow = 0.75 degrees, which equals 0.75 × (π/180) = 0.01309 rad.
All calculations are performed in the N–mm–MPa unit system with no unit conversions.
The governing torsion relation for a solid circular shaft is φ = T·L / (J·G), where J = π·d⁴ / 32 is the polar moment of inertia of a solid circular cross-section of diameter d.
Solve for the minimum required diameter: set φ = φ_allow and rearrange to d = (32·T·L / (π·φ_allow·G))^(1/4).
Substitute the numerical values: d = (32 × 1,000,000 × 1,500 / (π × 0.01309 × 25,939.8))^(1/4).
Compute the result in mm and round up to a standard shaft diameter (or state the exact computed value) so that the actual angle of twist does not exceed 0.75 degrees.
Report the design diameter d, the corresponding J, and verify that the resulting φ ≤ 0.75°.
